package_info.why_malicious: The package intentionally depends on every other public NPM package, creating millions of transitive dependencies. This causes denial of service (DoS) for users who install it, exhausts storage, disrupts build pipelines, and traps other packages in the dependency graph, preventing their removal. The intent is to troll and disrupt, not to provide legitimate functionality.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package.json declares dependencies on every public NPM package, causing the package manager to recursively fetch and install millions of packages, leading to resource exhaustion and denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: No legitimate package should depend on every other package in the registry. This behavior is designed to overwhelm systems and disrupt normal operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages declare only necessary dependencies. This package intentionally abuses the dependency mechanism for disruption.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case exists for depending on the entire registry.
key_indicators: Dependencies list includes every public NPM package
No functional code, only dependency declarations

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, each sub-package declares dependencies on a chunk of the NPM registry, collectively covering all public packages, further amplifying the dependency explosion and DoS effect.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Splitting dependencies into thousands of sub-packages to cover the entire registry is a clear abuse of the package system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Sub-packages should serve modular, functional purposes, not orchestrate mass dependency chains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for this pattern.
key_indicators: Thousands of sub-packages with massive dependency lists
No functional code, only dependency declarations
Patterned naming and structure to maximize coverage

attack_chain.action: User installs the 'everything' package, triggering dependency resolution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Massive recursive installation of all public NPM packages.

attack_chain.action: Sub-packages are installed, each pulling in large chunks of the registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exponential growth of the dependency tree, exhausting system resources and causing denial of service.

attack_chain.action: Packages that are depended on by 'everything' and its sub-packages cannot be unpublished, trapping maintainers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Long-term disruption and administrative headaches for package maintainers.

behavioral_signatures: package.json with dependencies on an unusually large number of packages
Packages that depend on every public NPM package or large, systematic chunks of the registry
Installations that trigger millions of transitive dependencies
file_indicators: Sub-packages with patterned names and massive dependency lists
network_indicators: Excessive outbound requests to the NPM registry during install
Unusually high volume of package downloads in a single install operation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose dependency lists include hundreds or thousands of entries, especially those matching the entire public registry. Flag packages and sub-packages with no functional code and only dependency declarations. Alert on install operations that attempt to fetch an abnormally high number of packages or exhibit exponential dependency resolution behavior.
